name: issue_827_sleep_window_floor_mismatch
description: Issue #827 GAP-5 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). Overnight, the nearest-edge selector must compare indoor against the already-resolved SLEEP band (sleep_heat 60F / sleep_cool 72F), not the flat daytime comfort_heat (68F). Three readings in the sleep window on a warm day (margin m = 2F): 70F is in the cooling zone, so cool is armed at the sleep ceiling (72); 64F is 4F below the daytime floor but strictly between sleep floor + m (62F) and sleep ceiling - m (70F), so the sleep-window mode is kept and heat is NOT commanded at 68; 61F is still above the sleep floor (not a breach) but inside the sleep heat zone, so heat is armed at the SLEEP floor (60F, event floor_f=60, breach=false), not 68F. Rewritten for #1066 review: the old 22:40 assertion (ceiling 72) did not distinguish the sleep floor from the daytime floor. The isolated 64F case is asserted strongly by issue_827_sleep_window_interior_keeps_sleep_mode.json.
source: Issue #827 Design table, GAP-5 -- the resolver previously read a flat, non-sleep-aware comfort_heat.
notes: Occupant impact: overnight the home has a deliberately deeper setback (60F floor). A thermostat that used the daytime 68F floor would run the furnace at 64F, fighting the sleep setback and wasting energy while the occupant sleeps comfortably; one that never used the sleep floor would leave the house to fall below 60F.

Margin: m = comfort_deadband_warm_f (2F) raised to >= 2 and clamped to one third of the sleep band width (12F / 3 = 4F), so m = 2F: sleep heat zone <= 62F, cooling zone >= 70F, interior 62-70F. Day type is 'warm' deliberately: on a hot day m would be min(5, 4) = 4F and 64F would fall in the heat zone, blurring the case. Classification hvac_mode=off / windows_recommended=true are what classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_WARM.

Harness limits: the decision timeline records only the first decision, and no assertion type can say 'heat not commanded between T1 and T2'. The 64F case in this file is therefore only band-edge evidence (expect_band); the 61F case is strong (event payload floor_f=60, breach=false, last_hvac_mode=heat). The isolated 64F case lives in issue_827_sleep_window_interior_keeps_sleep_mode.json, where whole-run hvac_mode_never_commanded(heat) and comfort_family=cooling are meaningful.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: if the selector read the daytime comfort_heat (68F) instead of the resolved band.floor (60F), the 64F reading would be a breach and arm heat at 68F, so the first switch to heating would carry breach=true / floor_f=68 at 22:50; the 23:10 assertion (event comfort_family_switch with breach=false, floor_f=60) would fail because no genuine switch happens at 23:10. If nearest-edge arming were deleted entirely (origin/main), a warm day is natively cooling and heat is against-grain, needing a breach beyond the 2F deadband plus recency and a 90 s sustain: 61F (above the sleep floor) would not switch to heating at all, so the comfort_family_switch event, comfort_family=heating and last_hvac_mode=heat assertions all fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('evaluated against the resolved band [floor, ceiling] ... sleep/away/vacation-aware'; heat at or below floor + m).

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: either the furnace runs overnight at 68F against a 60F sleep setback (energy waste, a warmer bedroom than chosen) or the sleep floor is not defended and the house drifts below it.

events.note: In the sleep window (22:35 is after sleep_time 22:30). Indoor 70F, inside the sleep band [60F, 72F] and at ceiling - m (72 - 2 = 70F): cooling zone.

Warm-day classification (classifier derives hvac_mode=off, windows recommended). Sleep window: select_comfort_band() arms floor=sleep_heat(60), ceiling=sleep_cool(72). Indoor 70F is in the cooling zone, so cool is armed at the sleep ceiling (72).

Indoor 64F: 4F below the DAYTIME comfort_heat(68) but 4F above the sleep floor (60) and above sleep floor + m (62). Strictly between the margins, so the thermostat keeps its current mode (cool at 72). A selector that read the daytime floor would see a breach here and command heat at 68.
Re-evaluation at 64F: no heat at 68 (or anywhere); the sleep-window cool ceiling (72) stays armed.
Indoor 61F: still above the sleep floor (60F) so NOT a breach, but inside the sleep heat zone (<= 60 + 2 = 62F). The selector arms heat at the SLEEP floor (60), not the daytime floor (68).
Re-evaluation at 61F: heat armed at 60F (sleep floor).

assertions.reason: Baseline: sleep window is active -- the sleep band [60F, 72F] is armed, not the daytime band [68F, 74F].

At 64F (inside the sleep band, below the daytime floor) the armed band is still the sleep band [60F, 72F]. Band edges only: this proves no daytime band was re-armed; the family itself is asserted strongly in issue_827_sleep_window_interior_keeps_sleep_mode.json.
The heat arm at 61F uses the sleep floor 60, not the daytime floor 68: the most recent sent band event has floor=60.

The switch to heating is a NON-breach arm (indoor 61F is above the sleep floor 60F) computed against floor_f=60 (the resolved sleep floor), proving the selector's floor input is band.floor, not the daytime comfort_heat. With the daytime floor 68F the same reading would be a breach.
Final engine state: heating family armed at the sleep floor.
The last climate command is heat (the 60F sleep-floor setpoint), not a 68F daytime heat command.

verdict.summary: Overnight nearest-edge arming uses the sleep-resolved floor: heat is armed at the sleep floor (60F) from 61F, and never at the daytime floor (68F).
verdict.observed_behavior: 70F arms cool at 72; 64F keeps the sleep-window cool edge; 61F arms heat as a non-breach switch against floor_f=60 and commands heat at 60F.
verdict.expected_behavior: The selector's floor/ceiling inputs are the already-resolved band edges (sleep-aware overnight), never a raw daytime config value.
